What is your favorite keto treat that takes less than 15 min to make?

Mine are fatbombs. i take 200 grams of butter 200 grams of coconut oil and 150 grams of dark (87%) chocolate. I then melt all of them and pour the mixture into cupcake forms. After I put them in the freezer. Really nice, especially in summer.
Goddamn, how did I never hear of these. Been craving chocolate for so long now!

Mine differ in that I use powdered dark cocoa, and use almond butter in the mixture. I leave an almond butter and coconut oil blend sans chocolate off to the side to layer onto it for a little almond butter cup action.
Sprinkle parmesan cheese on a baking sheet topped with pepper or paprika. Bake 'em for a few mins and let cool. They are delicious to munch on.

Pepperoni with a dab of cream cheese smeared on it, then microwaved for about ten seconds. I often skip the microwaving part, though. It just adds to the extra nomness of it.

Shakes of all kinds! I have troubles reaching my protein most days, so my shakes usually involve a scoop of chocolate protein powder (Or cocoa powder and some stevia when I have reached my protein macro), 1 cup almond milk, 1 oz spinach, and 1 tbsp peanut butter. Sometimes I will mess around and add cream cheese, an espresso shot, vanilla, torani sugar free syrups, etc.

I've posted this elsewhere, but it's so versatile. http://www.genaw.com/lowcarb/cheezits.html

We make the "cracker" like this, but we also take 2 whole slices of cheese, place on opposite ends of a piece of parchment paper and nuke them for about a minute. Once done, coat with mayo or mustard on the flat side and make a sandwich, complete with another slice of cheese. Place in a container, or wrap in plastic, and refrigerate. By lunchtime you'll have perfectly pliable, but not mushy, "bread" on your sandwich. We make them the night before and transport them in the sandwich-sized plastic containers and they are perfect.

Cheese shells.

Place your favorite shredded cheese in a frying pan, maybe a but of your preferred fat to minimize sticking, and you're done. Leave them flat and add meats to make a mini pizza, make taco shells, or wrap a sausage or frank in that sucker while it's still pliable.

Introduce yourself, talk about anything, talk about your anxiety!

Hi, I'm squirrelbait. I'm almost into my late-20s, female. I've been actively dealing with my disorder since I was 19 when I figured out what was "wrong" with me. After bringing it to light in my family and conversations with (many) therapists, it has been determined that I have probably had it my whole life. My mother is a narcissit and my father is neglectful, but I have happily dealt with most of the issue of my nurtured anxiety.

Right now I feel myself facing a lot of difficulty. Even though I have made a lot of progress over the years and only have about 1 or 2 full-fledged panic attacks a year, I find the day-to-day things getting substantially harder. It's easy to throw myself into the big stuff like socializing with people I just met or going on a backpacking trip because I know it's only temporary, but the things like working every day, going to the doctor's, making friends....especially the making friends part. I know making friends as an adult is always hard, but I feel it is so much hard when you have a mini-anxiety attack while driving and almost cause an accident with someone in the car. Something that, while it happens frequently for you, ways so much more when there is another person around. Or how your words sometimes don't come out right and you hope people just don't notice, but then you're too nervous to talk. That feeling like you have embarrassed yourself beyond repair and no one will ever want to talk to you again once it happens. That is my current struggle. I am in therapy, but only once a week.

edit: My therapist is talking about putting me into group therapy to help with my issues around relating to people. I don't even call it social anxiety because i have absolutely no issues being social when I meet people, just after we've exchanged contact information and agreed to hang out in the future.
Do you think group therapy will be helpful? I definitely understand the anxiety about day-to-day.

Most of my issues in forming connections come from a fear of opening myself to others as I am so often judged when I do. I think group therapy will help me practice being myself around others without judgement so that I can be myself in public with judgement.

but I feel it is so much hard when you have a mini-anxiety attack while driving and almost cause an accident with someone in the car. Something that, while it happens frequently for you, ways so much more when there is another person around. Or how your words sometimes don't come out right and you hope people just don't notice, but then you're too nervous to talk. That feeling like you have embarrassed yourself beyond repair and no one will ever want to talk to you again once it happens.

Well, I feel for your troubles. I recently realized that this is why I developed a lot of different behaviors related to friendship situations. I see my anxiety as a barrier to new people and experiences. Good for you in getting yourself on the first steps in naming the problem. It took me a long time to figure this out without therapists, but hopefully this is a problem that can be overcome.
